entries.title: Primality testing: trial division vs AKS

algorithms.name: trial division
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(sqrt(N)) = Theta(2^(n/2)) divisions in the worst case (N prime)

algorithms.name: AKS
algorithms.time_complexity: Õ(n^(21/2)) as proven in AKS 2004 (Õ(n^(15/2)) using Fouvry's theorem); Õ(n^6) for the Lenstra-Pomerance variant

entries.title: Assignment problem: permutation enumeration vs the Hungarian method

algorithms.name: permutation enumeration
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n * n!) (n! permutations, Theta(n) to cost each)

algorithms.name: Hungarian method (shortest augmenting paths with potentials)
algorithms.time_complexity: O(n^3) worst case: the search for the i-th inserted row runs at most i iterations of its main loop, because every iteration except the last selects a column that is already matched (the loop stops at the first free column selected), the selected columns are distinct, and only i - 1 columns are matched at that time; iteration t evaluates one reduced cost for each of the n - t + 1 columns not yet selected and does Theta(n) further work. Hence at most n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 reduced-cost evaluations and O(n^3) time on every input. Theta(n^3) growth measured on the column-dominant family used for timing (no proof of that lower bound is given here)

entries.title: Determinant over GF(p): cofactor expansion vs Gaussian elimination

algorithms.name: Laplace (cofactor) expansion
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n!) field operations (n!/k! recursion nodes with k columns left, Theta(k^2) work each; n! * sum_k k^2/k! = Theta(n!))

algorithms.name: Gaussian elimination mod p
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) field operations on non-singular input (~n^3/3 multiply-subtracts); O(n^3) always (it can stop early on a singular matrix)

entries.title: Edit (Levenshtein) distance: plain recursion vs Wagner-Fischer DP

lower_bounds.bound: no O(n^(2-eps)) algorithm for any eps > 0
lower_bounds.setting: conditional on the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH)
lower_bounds.source: Backurs & Indyk 2015

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(D(n, n)) = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)) ~ Theta(5.83^n / sqrt(n)), D = Delannoy numbers: the calls d(i, j) with i = n or j = n are the leaves, and the root-to-leaf paths are the lattice paths from (0, 0) with steps (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) stopped at their first point with i = n or j = n; each extends in exactly one way to (n, n), so there are D(n, n) leaves, and since every other call has 3 children the recursion makes exactly (3 D(n, n) - 1)/2 calls. D(n, n) = sum_k C(n, k)^2 2^k = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)): by Stirling its largest term, near k = (2 - sqrt 2) n, is Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / n), and summing the Theta(sqrt n) terms around it gives the 1/sqrt(n) factor (standard Laplace estimate; sketched, not written out here)

algorithms.name: Wagner-Fischer dynamic programming
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) (Theta(|a| |b|) in general)

entries.title: Fibonacci numbers: naive recursion vs dynamic programming vs fast doubling

algorithms.name: naive recursion
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(phi^n), phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 ~ 1.618

algorithms.name: bottom-up dynamic programming
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n) word operations

algorithms.name: fast doubling (matrix power)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(log n) word operations

entries.title: Greatest common divisor: trial divisors vs Euclid's algorithm

algorithms.name: trial divisors
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(2^n) iterations in the worst case: exactly min(a, b) - gcd(a, b) + 1 iterations of one or two divisions, i.e. up to 2^n - 2 on coprime n-bit inputs (>= 2^(n-2) on the coprime Fibonacci pairs used for V2: the pair is F_(k+1), F_k with F_(k+1) < 2^n <= F_(k+2), and F_(k+2) = F_(k+1) + F_k <= 3 F_k, so min(a, b) = F_k >= 2^n / 3 > 2^(n-2)). In bit operations, Theta(2^n) times the cost of an n-bit division.

algorithms.name: Euclid's algorithm
algorithms.time_complexity: O(n) division steps: at most log_phi(min(a, b)) + O(1) <= 1.44 n + O(1) (Lame 1844), attained by consecutive Fibonacci numbers. O(n^2) bit operations with schoolbook division: a step with quotient q on numbers of at most n bits costs O(n (1 + log q)), and the log q sum to at most n; Theta(n^2) on consecutive Fibonacci numbers, where each of the Theta(n) steps divides Theta(n)-bit numbers.

entries.title: Global minimum cut: all bipartitions vs Stoer-Wagner

algorithms.name: brute force
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2 2^n): exactly n(n-1)2^(n-3) weight additions and 2^(n-1) - 2 weight comparisons (n >= 2). In terms of the input size N = n^2 entries this is 2^Theta(sqrt(N)), still super-polynomial.

algorithms.name: Stoer-Wagner (array)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) with plain arrays: a phase on k vertices costs Theta(k^2); exactly (n-1)(n-2)(n+3)/6 weight additions and n(n-1)(n-2)/6 + n - 2 weight comparisons (n >= 2).

entries.title: Horn-SAT: brute force over all assignments vs linear-time unit propagation

algorithms.name: brute force over all assignments
algorithms.time_complexity: O(2^n * L) always; Theta(2^n * n) = Theta(2^n * m) on the V2 family H_n, where every assignment is examined (unsatisfiable) and the 2^(n-1) assignments with x1 false pass n - 2 clauses before failing: exactly (2n + 13) 2^(n-2) - 2n - 4 literal evaluations.

algorithms.name: unit propagation with clause counters (Dowling-Gallier)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + L) on every input: every variable is set true at most once, so every negative literal occurrence is decremented at most once and every clause fires at most once. On H_n exactly 12n - 7 counted operations.

algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3)

entries.title: Interval DP with inclusion-monotone weights (endpoint law; maximum-cost BST): plain recursion vs cubic DP vs endpoint DP

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(3^n) on every input: exactly 3^n calls and (3^(n-1) - 1)/2 cost comparisons for n >= 1

algorithms.name: cubic interval DP (every root)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) on every input: n(n+1)(n+2)/6 candidate roots, (n+1)n(n-1)/6 cost comparisons

algorithms.name: endpoint DP (two candidate roots per interval)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) on every input: n(n+1)/2 intervals with O(1) work each; exactly n(n-1)/2 cost comparisons

bases: Qian, J.; Wang, C. A. (2004). Maximum weight triangulation of a special convex polygon. 20th European Workshop on Computational Geometry (EWCG 2004), Seville. http://hdl.handle.net/11441/55702. Lemma 1.
provenance.note: The endpoint law for inclusion-monotone interval weights follows by the exchange argument of the cited lemma.

entries.title: Maximum-weight independent set on k x n grids with diagonals: exhaustive search vs DP over a path decomposition

algorithms.name: exhaustive search over all vertex subsets
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(N 2^N) on every input (N = k n), i.e. 2^Theta(n) for every fixed k. Exactly N 2^(N-1) weight additions on every input: (3/2) n 8^n for k = 3 (the V2 family).

algorithms.name: DP over the columns (path decomposition of width 2k-1)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(F_{k+2}^2 n) = Theta(phi^(2k) n) word operations (F_{k+2}^2 compatibility tests per column; F_{k+2} = 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21 for k = 1..6): Theta(n) for every fixed k, exponential in k. Weight additions: exactly n P_k + (n-1) F_{k+2} on every instance with n >= 1 and positive weights, where P_k is the total number of rows over all column states; 10n - 5 for k = 3 (P_3 = 5, F_5 = 5), the V2 family.

entries.title: Minimum spanning tree: edge-subset enumeration vs Kruskal (and Prim)

algorithms.name: enumeration of all (n-1)-edge subsets
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n * C(n(n-1)/2, n-1)) = 2^Theta(n log n) (C(m, n-1) subsets, Theta(n) each to build, search and weigh)

algorithms.name: Kruskal with union-find
algorithms.time_complexity: O(m log m) = O(n^2 log n) on K_n (comparison sort of the m edges; the union-find work is O(m alpha(n)))

algorithms.name: Prim, array version
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) on K_n (n-1 rounds, two Theta(n) scans each), linear in the input size

entries.title: Modular exponentiation: repeated multiplication vs square-and-multiply

lower_bounds.bound: at least ceil(log2 e) >= n - 1 multiplications (each multiplication at most doubles the largest exponent computed so far)
lower_bounds.setting: addition-chain (multiplication-only) model: each step multiplies two powers of a computed earlier
lower_bounds.source: Knuth TAOCP Vol. 2 (1997), 4.6.3

algorithms.name: repeated multiplication
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(e) = Theta(2^n) multiplications mod m (exactly e of them, and e >= 2^(n-1))

algorithms.name: left-to-right square-and-multiply (binary method)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n) multiplications mod m: n squarings plus one multiplication per 1-bit of e (at most n), and Theta(n) work to read the bits of e

entries.title: Optimal binary search tree: plain recursion vs cubic DP vs Knuth's quadratic DP

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(3^n) on every input: exactly 3^n calls (n >= 0) and (3^(n-1) - 1)/2 cost comparisons (n >= 1)

algorithms.name: cubic interval DP (every root)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) on every input: n(n+1)(n+2)/6 candidate roots, (n+1)n(n-1)/6 cost comparisons

algorithms.name: Knuth's speed-up (monotone roots)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) on every input. Upper bound: for each length L >= 2 the range widths telescope, sum_i (r[i+1][i+L] - r[i][i+L-1] + 1) = (n - L + 1) + r[n-L+1][n] - r[0][L-1] <= 2n - L; lower bound: n(n+1)/2 intervals, each doing at least one candidate. Exactly sum_{L=2..n} (r[n-L+1][n] - r[0][L-1]) <= (n-1)^2 cost comparisons, with equality on the V2 family (two heavy end keys) for n >= 1.

entries.title: Weighted perfect matchings of planar grid graphs (dimers): backtracking enumeration vs Kasteleyn's signed determinant (Bareiss)

algorithms.name: backtracking enumeration of perfect matchings
algorithms.time_complexity: O(N 2^(N/2)) on every instance: the search tree has branching factor <= 2 and depth <= N/2, and the scan for the next unmatched vertex only moves forward along a root-to-leaf path. The time is also at least the number of perfect matchings, which is exponential in N for unit weights: F(N/2 + 1) = Theta(phi^(N/2)) (Fibonacci numbers) on the (N/2) x 2 ladder, and at least 2^(N/4) on a x b grids with a and b even (N/4 disjoint 2 x 2 blocks with 2 tilings each). Counted cost (one multiplication weight * subtotal per search-tree edge) on the V2 family, the unit-weight (n/2) x 2 ladder: Theta(phi^(n/2)) = Theta(1.272^n), exactly L(n/2 + 2) - 3 = phi^(n/2+2) + (-1/phi)^(n/2+2) - 3 multiplications (L = Lucas numbers). On the 2 x (n/2) ladder (the same graph, vertices numbered along the long side) it is Theta(n phi^(n/2)), see caveats.

algorithms.name: Kasteleyn signed determinant with Bareiss fraction-free elimination
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(N^3) arithmetic operations: exactly (m-1) m (2m-1)/2 = (N-2) N (N-1)/8 multiplications and exact divisions (m = N/2) on every instance with a non-zero answer, whatever row swaps occur (the loops do not depend on the values unless a column is zero from the pivot down, which forces det = 0); at most that many when the answer is 0, none for odd N; plus Theta(N^2) entry reads and negations to build K. The integers are not of constant size: every Bareiss value is a minor of K (rows permuted), at most (2 w_max)^(N/2) in absolute value by Hadamard's inequality (each row of K has at most 4 non-zero entries, so Euclidean norm <= 2 w_max), and a product before division is at most 2 (2 w_max)^N in absolute value, so all values have O(N log(2 w_max)) bits. Bit complexity O(N^3 M(N log(2 w_max))), where M(b) is the cost of multiplying b-bit integers: polynomial in the input size.

entries.title: Regular-expression matching: backtracking vs memoised backtracking vs Thompson's NFA simulation

algorithms.name: backtracking (consume first)
algorithms.time_complexity: Exponential in the worst case. On P_n exactly (n + 2) * 2^(n-1) - 1 symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n * 2^n). In general O(2^(m + |t|)): every call makes at most two recursive calls and each increases i + j, so the call tree has depth <= m + |t| + 1.

algorithms.name: memoised backtracking
algorithms.time_complexity: O((m + 1)(|t| + 1)) subproblems with O(1) work each (expected O(1) dictionary operations), i.e. O(n^2) for the stated n. On P_n exactly n(n + 1) symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n^2).

algorithms.name: Thompson's NFA simulation
algorithms.time_complexity: O(m (|t| + 1)): at most m + 1 states per step with O(1) work each, plus an O(m) closure per step; O(n^2) for the stated n. On P_n exactly n(n + 1) symbol-character comparisons, Theta(n^2).

entries.title: Single-pair shortest path: simple-path enumeration vs Dijkstra

algorithms.name: simple-path enumeration
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n (n-2)!) on the complete digraph (~ e (n-2)! simple s-t paths, n neighbour checks per search node)

algorithms.name: Dijkstra (array version)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) with an array (linear in the n x n weight-matrix input; it reads exactly n(n-1)/2 distinct weights, for each pair of vertices the one leaving the vertex settled first), which is optimal up to a constant factor for weight-matrix input: for n >= 4 split the n - 2 vertices other than s, t into U (floor((n-2)/2) of them) and W, and set w(s, u) = 1, w(u, x) = 2 and w(x, t) = 1 for u in U, x in W, all other weights 100; then dist(s, t) = 4, and lowering any one weight w(u, x) to 1 makes it 3, so on this instance every correct deterministic algorithm (and every run of a zero-error randomized one) reads all floor((n-2)^2/4) weights w(u, x). O(m + n log n) with Fibonacci heaps

entries.title: Counting spanning trees: edge-subset enumeration vs Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem (Bareiss)

algorithms.name: enumeration of all (n-1)-edge subsets
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2) to read the matrix, plus C(m, n-1) subsets at Theta(n) each to reset the union-find arrays and at most n-1 unions (2(n-1) finds; O(n alpha(n)) amortized with union by size and path halving): O(n alpha(n) C(m, n-1)) and Omega(n C(m, n-1)). C(m, n-1) grows with m, so the worst case is K_n, m = n(n-1)/2: (n/2)^(n-1) <= C(n(n-1)/2, n-1) <= (e n/2)^(n-1), i.e. 2^Theta(n log n), super-exponential in n.

algorithms.name: Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem with Bareiss fraction-free elimination
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) arithmetic operations: exactly (n-2)(n-1)(2n-3)/2 multiplications and exact divisions on every connected graph (no zero pivot occurs), at most that many otherwise (it stops at the first zero pivot), plus Theta(n^2) additions to build the Laplacian. The integers are not of constant size: every intermediate entry is a minor of the reduced Laplacian, of absolute value < n^(n-1) by Hadamard's inequality (each row has Euclidean norm <= sqrt(n(n-1)) < n), and a product before division is < 2 n^(2(n-1)), so all values have O(n log n) bits. Bit complexity O(n^3 M(n log n)), where M(b) is the cost of multiplying b-bit integers (O(n^5 log^2 n) with schoolbook multiplication): polynomial in the n^2-bit input.

entries.title: 2-SAT: brute force over all assignments vs implication graph + strongly connected components

algorithms.name: brute force over all assignments
algorithms.time_complexity: O(2^n * m) always; Theta(2^n * m) in the worst case (unsatisfiable formulas in which a constant fraction of the assignments pass Theta(m) clauses before failing, e.g. clauses all containing x1 followed by an unsatisfiable core). On the V2 family W_n (m = 2n + 2) exactly (n + 7) * 2^(n-1) + 2 literal evaluations = Theta(n * 2^n) = Theta(m * 2^n).

algorithms.name: Aspvall-Plass-Tarjan (implication graph + Tarjan SCC)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + m) (Theta(n) on the V2 family, where m = 2n + 2)

entries.title: XOR-SAT and #XOR-SAT: brute force over all assignments vs Gaussian elimination over GF(2)

algorithms.name: brute force over all assignments
algorithms.time_complexity: O(2^n * m * n) bit operations always; Theta(2^n * n) on systems whose rows are linearly independent (row i is reached by 2^(n-i) assignments), in particular exactly (2n + 1)(2^(n+1) - 2) counted operations on the V2 family X_n (and on every n x n system of full rank). The worst case Theta(2^n * m * n) needs many dependent rows (e.g. repeated equations).

algorithms.name: Gaussian elimination over GF(2)
algorithms.time_complexity: O(m n min(m, n)) bit operations; Theta(n^3) for n x n systems in the worst case: exactly n (n^2 + 6n - 4) / 3 counted operations on the V2 family X_n.

entries.title: All-pairs shortest paths on dense digraphs: Bellman-Ford from every source vs Floyd-Warshall

algorithms.name: Bellman-Ford from every source
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2 m) for m >= 1 edges (n sources x (n - 1) passes x m relaxations, no early exit), plus Theta(n^2) to list the edges: Theta(n^4) when m = Theta(n^2); exactly n^2 (n-1)^2 relaxations on the complete digraphs used for timing

algorithms.name: Floyd-Warshall
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) on every input (exactly n^3 relaxation steps; independent of m)

entries.title: Maximum bipartite matching: one augmenting path per vertex (Kuhn) vs Hopcroft-Karp

algorithms.name: Kuhn's augmenting paths (one DFS per left vertex)
algorithms.time_complexity: O(V (V + E)), i.e. O(V E) when E = Omega(V): one O(V + E) search per left vertex, and at most n_left E <= V E edge scans on every input (in one search a left vertex is pushed at most once, since the root is free and every other pushed vertex is the partner of a right vertex seen for the first time, and a pushed vertex reads each entry of its list at most once). On the adversarial family G_k (V = 4k^2 + k, E = 2k^4 + k^2) exactly (7k^6 + 9k^4 + 11k^2 - 3k)/6 edge scans for every k >= 1. Proof sketch, with a = k^2: before gadget root u < a, gadget left vertex i is matched to right vertex u - 1 - i (i < u), so the search from u runs through all u matched gadget vertices, reads (u + 1)(u + 2)/2 entries and succeeds; each of the other a gadget roots fails after reading a(a + 1) entries (its own list and the lists of the a matched gadget vertices); in path j the roots L_2..L_j read 1 entry each and L_1 reads 2j - 1, so path j costs 3j - 2. The sum C(a + 2, 3) + a^2 (a + 1) + k(3k - 1)/2 is the formula, and it equals the V2 counts listed under verification. So Kuhn makes Theta(V E) = Theta(V^3) scans on G_k; the ratio to V E tends to 7/48

algorithms.name: Hopcroft-Karp
algorithms.time_complexity: O((V + E) sqrt(V)): O(sqrt(V)) phases (Hopcroft & Karp 1973), O(V + E) each; O(V^2.5) on dense graphs (the paper's title bound). On the adversarial family G_k exactly k + 1 phases (k augmenting phases and a final search that finds no augmenting path) and (24k^5 + 9k^4 + 4k^3 + 24k^2 - 25k + 12)/6 = Theta(E sqrt V) edge scans for every k >= 1; the ratio to E sqrt V tends to 1. Proof sketch, with a = k^2: in phase 1 the breadth-first search reads all E entries, and the depth-first searches read a(a + 1)/2 + a^2 + k(k + 1)/2 entries, match all a gadget right vertices and path 1, and leave path j >= 2 with the j - 1 edges L_i R_(i-1) matched and L_1, R_j free; in phase t (2 <= t <= k) the target level is t, the breadth-first search reads 2a^2 entries in the gadget and 2t - 1 in each path j >= t, and the depth-first searches read 2a^2 in the gadget, 2t - 1 in path t, which they repair, and 2t + 1 in each later path, which they leave unchanged; phase k + 1 reads 2a^2 entries and finds no free right vertex. The per-phase counts sum to the formula, which equals the V2 counts listed under verification

algorithms.name: Karatsuba

algorithms.name: all pairs

algorithms.name: merge-sort counting

entries.title: Longest palindromic substring: brute force vs expanding around centers vs Manacher

algorithms.name: brute force (test every substring)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) worst case: on n equal characters every substring is a palindrome and the tests make sum_{L=1..n} (n-L+1) floor(L/2) ~ n^3/12 comparisons; Omega(n^2) on every input (n(n+1)/2 tests)

algorithms.name: expand around centers
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n + R) where R = sum of the maximal palindrome radii over all centers: Theta(n^2) worst case (n equal characters: n^2/2 + n/2 comparisons); Theta(n) in expectation on uniformly random strings over sigma >= 2 letters: at a centre, the r-th comparison between distinct positions is made only if the r - 1 before it succeeded, and these test equality at disjoint pairs of positions, independent events of probability 1/sigma each, so it is made with probability at most 2^-(r-1); hence a gap centre costs at most 2 comparisons in expectation and a character centre at most 3 (its first comparison is of the character with itself), at most 5n - 2 in total, and at least n

algorithms.name: Manacher's algorithm
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n) on every input (at most 2n successful comparisons and at most 2n failed ones)

algorithms.name: schoolbook
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3)

algorithms.name: Strassen
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^(log2 7)) ~ Theta(n^2.807)

algorithms.name: Edmonds-Karp

algorithms.name: Dinic (blocking flows)
algorithms.time_complexity: O(V^2 E): at most V - 1 phases, O(V E) per blocking flow; O(V^4) on dense graphs

entries.title: Maximum subarray sum: brute force vs running sums vs Kadane's scan

algorithms.name: brute force (sum every subarray)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) on every input: the innermost loop runs n(n+1)(n+2)/6 times

algorithms.name: running sums

entries.title: Multi-pattern string matching: naive matching per pattern vs KMP per pattern vs Aho-Corasick

algorithms.name: naive matching per pattern
algorithms.time_complexity: O(N L) character comparisons; Theta(sum over patterns of (N - m + 1) m) in the worst case. On the V2 family exactly sum_j j (n^2 - j + 1) = n(n+1)(3n^2 - 2n + 2)/6 comparisons = Theta(n^4) (each of the n^2 - j + 1 alignments of a^(j-1) b matches j - 1 characters and fails on the b).

algorithms.name: Knuth-Morris-Pratt per pattern
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(P N + L): Theta(N + m) per pattern (at most 3(m - 1) comparisons for the failure table and 3N for the scan: the implementation compares the current character again after the while loop, as in string-matching-naive-vs-kmp). On the V2 family exactly 3n^3 - 2n^2 - 5n + 6 comparisons for n >= 2 = Theta(n^3): pattern b costs N, pattern ab costs 2N, and a^(j-1) b for j >= 3 costs 3j - 6 (failure table) + 3N - j (scan), with N = n^2.

algorithms.name: Aho-Corasick
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(N + L) character comparisons for a fixed alphabet of sigma characters (children kept as lists scanned linearly, at most sigma comparisons per lookup; at most 2N lookups in the scan and O(L) in the construction; at least N + L - sigma comparisons, since every scan step ends with a lookup in a non-empty child list, at most T of the L insertion lookups find an empty list (T = number of trie nodes created), and every created node of depth >= 2 ends its failure-link search with a lookup in a non-empty list), independent of the number of occurrences. On the V2 family exactly 4n^2 - 3 comparisons for n >= 1 = Theta(n^2): (n-1)^2 to build the trie (inserting a^(j-1) b costs 2(j-2) + 1 comparisons for j >= 2, 0 for j = 1), 3n - 5 for the failure links (n >= 2: 1 for the b-child and 2 for the a-child of every a^d, d = 1..n-1, the a-child only for d <= n-2), and 3n^2 - n + 1 for the scan (n >= 2; 2 per character down the a-chain for the first n - 1 characters, then 3 per character: the b-only node a^(n-1) fails, its failure link a^(n-2) has the a-child at the second position).

entries.title: 3XOR: all triples vs a Patricia trie (deterministic quadratic)

algorithms.name: all triples
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3) in the worst case. Exactly, on every instance without a solution (the V2 family is one): C(n, 2) XORs and C(n, 3) equality tests, C(n, 2) + C(n, 3) = C(n + 1, 3) = (n^3 - n)/6 word operations (the middle loop runs once per pair, the inner loop once per triple; Pascal's rule sums the two binomials). With a solution it stops at the first hit.

algorithms.name: Patricia trie
algorithms.time_complexity: O(n^2 + n w) word operations; Theta(n^2) in the worst case when w = O(n) (attained on the V2 family). The zero scan is n comparisons, the build at most n w bit tests (each index is tested once per bit until its group is a singleton), and each of the |D| <= n rounds costs O(|D|): |D| - 1 bit tests at branching nodes, |D| XORs and a merge of at most 2|D| - 1 steps. Exactly, on the V2 family (all w-bit words of odd Hamming weight, n = 2^(w-1), no solution): 7n^2 + 2n log2(n) - 3n operations. Derivation: n zero comparisons; the build tests every word once at each of the bits w-1..1 (a group fixed on its top bits holds all suffixes of one parity, 2^(r-1) words for r remaining bits, and splits at the next bit while r >= 2; at r = 1 it is a single word), n(w - 1) = n log2(n) bit tests of 2 operations each (AND, truth test), and the trie has n leaves and n - 1 branching nodes; per a: 2(n - 1) for the bit tests at branching nodes, n XORs, and the merge: {a XOR x} is the set of even-weight words, which interleaves with the odd-weight words (each pair 2t, 2t + 1 holds one of each), so the merge consumes every word up to 2^w - 2, 2n - 1 steps of one equality test and one less-than test, 4n - 2; per a 7n - 4. Total n + 2n log2(n) + n(7n - 4).

algorithms.name: subset DP over all independent sets
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(3^n) on every input: exactly 3^n - 2^n inner iterations (one per pair T, S with T a non-empty subset of S), plus Theta(2^n) to tabulate the independent subsets

algorithms.name: inclusion-exclusion (Bjorklund-Husfeldt-Koivisto)
algorithms.time_complexity: (2 chi(G) + 2) 2^n - 2 arithmetic operations: one pass of two additions per non-empty subset to tabulate a, then chi(G) rounds of one multiplication and one addition per subset. The integers have at most n chi(G) bits. That is O(n 2^n) arithmetic operations in the unit-cost model (chi(G) <= n), Theta(n 2^n) whenever chi(G) = Theta(n), and O(n^4 2^n) bit operations with schoolbook multiplication

entries.title: Ordering a first-match rule list: enumeration of all k! orders vs dynamic programming over subsets of rules

algorithms.name: enumeration of all orders
algorithms.time_complexity: O(k! k m): k! orders, at most k match tests per item, one addition per item. On the V2 family (m = k, item i matched by rules i and i+1 mod k) exactly k! (k+1)(k+3)/3 - 1 counted operations = Theta(k! k^2) = Theta(k! k m): k! k(k+1)/3 truth tests (the earlier of an item's two rules stands on average at position (k+1)/3 of a random order: P(min >= j) = C(k-j+1, 2)/C(k, 2), summed over j = 1..k this is C(k+1, 3)/C(k, 2)), k! k additions and k! - 1 comparisons (none for the first order).

algorithms.name: dynamic programming over subsets of rules
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(2^k (k + m)) on every input: per subset m capture tests and k - |S| transitions; an item matched by t >= 1 rules is uncaptured for 2^(k-t) subsets and then adds t costs, and t 2^(k-t) <= 2^(k-1). Exactly 3k^2 + (7k - 2) 2^(k-1) + 2 counted operations on the V2 family (k >= 2): 3km = 3k^2 for building the rule lists (k truth tests per item) and the masks (k shifts and k additions per item); 2k 2^k for the capture tests (an & and a truth test per item and subset); k 2^(k-1) gain additions (each item is uncaptured for the 2^(k-2) subsets avoiding its two rules and then adds 2 costs); k 2^(k-1) transition additions; k 2^(k-1) - 2^k + 1 comparisons (a subset T is reached |T| times, the first arrival is stored without comparison); 1 final addition.

entries.title: Counting Hamiltonian cycles: permutation enumeration vs inclusion-exclusion (and the Held-Karp counting DP)

algorithms.name: permutation enumeration
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n!) arc tests in the worst case: exactly n! on the complete digraph with n >= 2 (the V2 family), where no test fails; at least (n-1)! orders are generated on every input.

algorithms.name: inclusion-exclusion over vertex subsets
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^3 2^n). Exactly, on every input with n >= 1 vertices: n(n-1)(n+2)2^(n-3) multiplications and n(n-1)(n+2)2^(n-3) + 2^(n-1) - 1 additions/subtractions, in total n(n-1)(n+2)2^(n-2) + 2^(n-1) - 1 operations (for |T| = t the DP makes n steps of t(t-1) products and t(t-1) additions, and sum over S of (|S|+1)|S| = (n-1)(n+2)2^(n-3); the extra 2^(n-1) - 1 are the signed accumulations, the one for T = {0} adds a plain 0).

algorithms.name: Held-Karp counting DP
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(n^2 2^n). Exactly, on every input with n >= 1 vertices: (n-1)(n-2)2^(n-3) + (n-1) multiplications and as many additions, in total (n-1)(n-2)2^(n-2) + 2(n-1) operations (a set S of size s >= 2 costs s(s-1) products, sum over s of C(n-1, s) s(s-1) = (n-1)(n-2)2^(n-3), plus n-1 closing products).

entries.title: Bernstein-Vazirani: n classical queries vs 1 quantum query

lower_bounds.bound: n queries for every success probability > 1/2, randomized algorithms included
lower_bounds.source: Proved in this entry: for a uniformly random s, the answers s.x_1, ..., s.x_q to q queries (chosen adaptively) leave s uniform on the solutions of q linear equations over GF(2), an affine subspace of dimension >= n - q, so a deterministic q-query algorithm outputs s with probability at most 2^(q-n). Averaging over its coins, every randomized q-query algorithm also succeeds with probability at most 2^(q-n) on average over s, hence on some s; success > 1/2 on every s therefore needs q >= n. The problem is from Bernstein & Vazirani 1997

algorithms.name: classical: query the unit vectors
algorithms.time_complexity: n queries (optimal classically, also for randomized algorithms that succeed with probability > 1/2)

algorithms.name: Bernstein-Vazirani quantum algorithm
algorithms.time_complexity: 1 query (O(n) gates besides the oracle)

entries.title: Collision problem: Theta(N^(1/2)) classical queries vs Theta(N^(1/3)) quantum queries (Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp)

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(sqrt N) = Omega(2^(n/2)) queries for bounded error
lower_bounds.source: Birthday argument: on a uniformly random 2-to-1 function, after i collision-free queries ANY next query completes a pair with probability exactly i/(N-i), so q queries reveal a collision with probability at most q^2/(2(N-q)), and guessing an unseen pair succeeds with probability at most 1/(N-q-1); Yao's principle gives the randomized bound. Stated as the classical optimum (expected Theta(sqrt N)) in the arXiv note of Brassard, Hoyer & Tapp (1997). It also follows from the classical lower bound for Simon's problem (simon-classical-vs-quantum), because every Simon instance is 2-to-1 and any collision reveals s.

lower_bounds.bound: N/2 + 1 queries in the worst case for algorithms that are always correct (N >= 4)
lower_bounds.source: Elementary adversary argument: answer the first N/2 queries with distinct values; every unqueried point can still be the partner of every queried one, so no pair is certain. Pigeonhole makes N/2 + 1 sufficient.

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(N^(1/3)) = Omega(2^(n/3)) queries for bounded error (BHT is optimal up to a constant factor)
lower_bounds.setting: query (oracle) model, unconditional; proven for the decision version (1-to-1 vs 2-to-1), which the search version solves with one extra check
lower_bounds.source: Aaronson & Shi 2004 (proof requires a codomain of size at least 3N/2, which this harness's codomain of size 2N satisfies; as stated by Kutin 2005); Kutin 2005 and Ambainis 2005 remove the range condition

algorithms.name: classical birthday search
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(sqrt N) = Theta(2^(n/2)) queries expected: E[Q] = sum_q prod_{i=1}^{q-1} (N-2i)/(N-i) ~ sqrt(pi N / 2) (each factor is 1 - i/(N - i) = exp(-i/N + O(i^2/N^2)), so the q-th term is exp(-q^2/(2N) + o(1)) uniformly for q <= N^0.6; the at most N/2 + 1 later terms are each smaller than the term at q = N^0.6, which is exp(-N^0.2/2 + o(1)), so they add o(1); and the sum over q >= 1 of exp(-q^2/(2N)) is (1 + o(1)) sqrt(pi N / 2), a Riemann sum of the Gaussian integral); at most N/2 + 1

algorithms.name: Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp, known number of marked points
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(N^(1/3)) = Theta(2^(n/3)) queries expected: k + (2m + 1)/sin^2((2m+1) theta) with sin^2 theta = k/N, m = floor(pi/(4 theta)), counting 2 queries per Grover iteration; about 2.57 N^(1/3)

algorithms.name: Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp with BBHT exponential search (unknown number of marked points)
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(N^(1/3)) queries expected (BBHT Theorem 3: O(sqrt(N/t)) iterations for t marked items); exact expectation about 3.9 N^(1/3) for large N, reached only for n >~ 18

entries.title: Deutsch-Jozsa: 2^(n-1)+1 exact classical queries vs 1 exact quantum query (no gap once classical error is allowed)

lower_bounds.bound: 2^(n-1) + 1 queries in the worst case, for any algorithm that is always correct
lower_bounds.setting: query (oracle) model, EXACT (zero-error) computation, unconditional. The same argument forces 2^(n-1) + 1 queries on every constant input for zero-error randomized (Las Vegas) algorithms. It does NOT hold for bounded-error randomized algorithms, which need only O(1) queries (see the randomized algorithm in this entry).
lower_bounds.source: Elementary adversary argument: answer f(x) = 0 to the first 2^(n-1) distinct queries; both the constant-0 function and a balanced function (ones on unqueried points only) remain consistent, so no exact algorithm can stop. Spelled out in this entry's correctness fields and README; the comparison with exact deterministic computation goes back to Deutsch & Jozsa 1992.

entries.title: Element distinctness: Theta(N) classical queries vs Theta(N^(2/3)) quantum queries (Ambainis quantum walk)

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(N) queries for bounded error
lower_bounds.source: Elementary reduction from the OR function on N - 1 bits (randomized query complexity Theta(N)): set x_0 = 0 and x_i = i if y_i = 0, x_i = 0 if y_i = 1; the values are all distinct iff OR(y) = 0, and each query of x costs at most one query of y.

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(N^(2/3)) queries for bounded error (Ambainis's algorithm is optimal up to a constant factor)
lower_bounds.source: Aaronson & Shi 2004 (from the collision lower bound; Shi's abstract: 'implies a quantum lower bound of Omega(n^(2/3)) queries ... for the element distinctness problem'); Ambainis 2005 extends it to small ranges (all M >= N)
